{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Feasible as a single-column ELM elevation-gradient experiment; water-partitioning fluxes are model diagnostics and USGS gauges provide runoff validation.",
    "answerable": [
      "Contrast of ET, runoff, drainage, and snow storage between wet (1993) and dry (2002) years",
      "Elevation control on rain/snow partitioning and snowmelt-driven runoff",
      "Relative role of forcing anomaly vs elevation in water partitioning"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Spatially distributed streamflow routing/hydrograph timing at the gauge (single-column has no lateral routing)",
      "Snowpack validation at columns (SNOTEL sparse/missing)",
      "Basin-integrated water budget closure without a routing/aggregation scheme"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "The domain spans 900-3300 m, and elevation is the primary candidate driver of rain/snow partitioning and ET. Three columns (low desert, mid transition, high snow-influenced) bracket the elevation range and let us separate the elevation control from the wet/dry forcing contrast without over-proliferating single-column runs.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "SRH_low_1000m", "lat": 33.55, "lon": -110.55, "soil_texture": "sandy loam"},
    {"id": "SRH_mid_2000m", "lat": 33.85, "lon": -110.10, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "SRH_high_3000m", "lat": 34.05, "lon": -109.75, "soil_texture": "gravelly loam"}

  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "18",

      "RAIN",

      "QVEGE",
      "QSOIL",
      "SOILWATER_10CM",
      "H2OSOI",
      "ZWT",
      "TWS",
      "TSA",
      "RH2M"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": ["elm_single_column", "datm_gswp3_forcing"],
  "assumptions": [
    "GSWP3/CRUNCEP forcing (1980-2018) is used; STOP_N=18 from 1985 provides ~8-yr spinup before the analysis years 1993 and 2002.",
    "Wet vs dry contrast is diagnosed from full water years 1993 (wet) and 2002 (dry) within the transient run.",
    "PFT/vegetation set from surface dataset at each lat/lon (desert shrub at low, mixed conifer/pinyon-juniper at mid/high).",
    "No lateral routing; runoff terms are treated as local generation, with USGS gauge used only for qualitative wet/dry-year anomaly comparison.",

feasibility.verdict: Feasible as a single-column ELM elevation-gradient experiment; water-partitioning fluxes are model diagnostics and USGS gauges provide runoff validation.
answerable: Contrast of ET, runoff, drainage, and snow storage between wet (1993) and dry (2002) years
Elevation control on rain/snow partitioning and snowmelt-driven runoff
Relative role of forcing anomaly vs elevation in water partitioning
not_answerable: Spatially distributed streamflow routing/hydrograph timing at the gauge (single-column has no lateral routing)

parsed.n_justification: The domain spans 900-3300 m, and elevation is the primary candidate driver of rain/snow partitioning and ET. Three columns (low desert, mid transition, high snow-influenced) bracket the elevation range and let us separate the elevation control from the wet/dry forcing contrast without over-proliferating single-column runs.
assumptions: GSWP3/CRUNCEP forcing (1980-2018) is used; STOP_N=18 from 1985 provides ~8-yr spinup before the analysis years 1993 and 2002.
Wet vs dry contrast is diagnosed from full water years 1993 (wet) and 2002 (dry) within the transient run.
PFT/vegetation set from surface dataset at each lat/lon (desert shrub at low, mixed conifer/pinyon-juniper at mid/high).
No lateral routing; runoff terms are treated as local generation, with USGS gauge used only for qualitative wet/dry-year anomaly comparison.
Model spun up to quasi-equilibrium soil moisture; if disequilibrium suspected, an accelerated-decomposition/AD spinup precedes the transient segment.
